name: Vantablack PA-1 'Pacifier'
description:
A rifle-format directed-energy weapon that fires a focused microwave beam at ranges up to 50 meters, heating the target's skin surface to create an intense burning sensation without causing visible injury. The Active Denial System technology was developed decades ago but miniaturized by Vantablack into a shoulder-fired platform that a single operator can carry and deploy. The Pacifier causes immediate reflexive retreat — the pain is so intense that targets abandon their position, drop held objects, and flee the beam path involuntarily.

Vantablack sells the PA-1 exclusively to corporate clients for crowd dispersal and perimeter defense. The weapon's appeal is its deniability — it causes extreme pain but leaves no marks, no wounds, and no forensic evidence. A crowd hit by Pacifier beams will disperse screaming, but medical examination will find nothing wrong with them. This makes the PA-1 the preferred tool for suppressing protests, demonstrations, and labor actions where visible casualties would create negative publicity.

The PA-1's limitations are well-documented but rarely discussed in marketing materials. The beam penetrates clothing to approximately 1/64th of an inch of skin depth, which means that metallic fabrics, wet clothing, or improvised reflective barriers significantly reduce effectiveness. The weapon also cannot distinguish between targets — the beam affects everyone in its path, including bystanders, children, and individuals with medical conditions that make heat exposure dangerous.
legality: Restricted — corporate security with crowd control authorization
specifications:
range: 50 meters effective
beam width: 2 meters at 30 meters
effect: Intense skin heating (54°C surface temperature)
power source: Heavy-duty battery pack, 30 minutes continuous operation
weight: 8.5 kg with battery
length: 900mm
tactical_use: Crowd dispersal, perimeter defense, and area denial. Operators sweep the beam across groups to force retreat. Effective against unarmed civilians and lightly equipped targets. Ineffective against prepared opponents with reflective or wet barrier materials.
cultural_context: The Pacifier is the weapon that labor organizers fear most — not because it is the most dangerous, but because it leaves no evidence. Workers hit by Pacifier beams during strike actions cannot prove they were attacked. Medical records show no injuries. Security footage shows people running away from nothing. The weapon's name is a cruel joke: it pacifies by causing invisible agony.
story_hooks: A Pacifier has been modified to operate at higher power, causing second-degree burns instead of surface heating. The modification makes the weapon's effects visible and documentable — someone is deliberately creating evidence of corporate violence that the original weapon was designed to conceal.

Medical researchers have identified a cluster of cancer cases in a district where Pacifier deployments were frequent during a prolonged labor dispute. Vantablack insists the technology is safe. The epidemiological data suggests otherwise.
related_entities: Carrion Defense Works Neural Lash NL-3 'Agony'

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, futuristic rifle with an unusually smooth profile — no visible cooling vents or conventional barrel. The emitter array is recessed slightly behind a flat, darkened faceplate that appears almost organic in its seamless integration. It has the predatory posture of a directed-energy platform, all forward momentum despite its lack of mechanical aggression.
physical_description.dimensions: 900mm total length, 65mm width at the receiver, 85mm height including integrated sights. Emitter dish face is approximately 120mm diameter.
physical_description.weight_description: Substantial and forward-heavy due to battery pack (8.5 kg total) — designed for supported firing from shoulder or bipod. The weight distribution demands control; it's not a weapon for sustained handheld operation without fatigue.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-composite chassis with aerospace-grade polymer skin. The emitter array housing is precision-molded aluminum with thermal dissipation fins concealed beneath the outer shell.
physical_description.finish: Deep matte black with a vantablack-coated emitter face that appears to absorb light almost completely — it looks like a void when viewed straight-on. Brushed metallic accents on the grip and control surfaces show intentional contrast.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant: absolute black. Accents: gunmetal gray and subtle amber warning striping along the power coupling and thermal management zones.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured rubberized polymer with subtle grip ridges — designed for gloved operation. The grip angle is aggressive, almost vertical, suggesting a platform meant for rapid targeting.
distinctive_features: Recessed emitter array with concentric thermal rings visible through translucent housing sections
Integrated LED status strip running along the left rail — green when operational, red when overheated or powered down
Heavy battery coupling at the rear with oversized connector — clearly modular design
Top-mounted aiming module with digital crosshair projection (not visible in passive mode)
Dual thermal vents along the barrel shroud, disguised as aesthetic ribbing
Vantablack corporate logo stamped near the power coupling — minimalist, almost invisible against the black finish
Serial plate in small numerals beneath the ejection port (corporate tracking requirement)
Wear-resistant polymer covering at the shoulder contact point, slightly discolored from repeated use
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Vantablack corporate logo appears as a subtle embossed icon near the battery coupling. Model designation 'PA-1' and 'PACIFIER' are printed in tiny white lettering on the left receiver rail. Serial number and corporate registration code stamped on a steel plate recessed into the lower chassis.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-worn but meticulously maintained by corporate security teams. The finish shows micro-scratches and scuff marks consistent with regular deployment and cleaning. The battery coupling shows signs of repeated mating cycles. The rubberized grip may show slight salt staining or wear polish from gloved hands.

image_prompt: Product photography of the Vantablack PA-1 Pacifier microwave dispersal rifle positioned on a matte dark gray surface, angled 45 degrees to show the recessed emitter array and thermal venting. Tactical gloved hand gripping the stock. Dramatic side-lighting from the left highlighting the brushed aluminum accents and the absolute black matte finish of the chassis, creating deep shadows that emphasize the recessed emitter void. Cool cyan accent lighting on the LED status strip. The emitter face should appear to absorb light unnaturally. Corporate environment background slightly blurred. Cyberpunk aesthetic with high contrast and clinical precision. --ar 3:2 --v 6
